output.summary: A biennial flowering plant native to Europe, western and central Asia, and north-western Africa, garlic mustard forms low leaf clusters in its first year and flowers the following spring. Its crushed leaves smell of garlic, while its small white flowers are cross-shaped and grow in dense clusters.
output.edibilityNote: Chopped leaves, especially young ones, flavour salads and sauces; flowers and fruit are sometimes included. Young first-year plants contain cyanide, whose gas is eliminated by chopping.
